minutes.headline: Charter Review Committee took no votes; it reviewed revised write-in wording, ranked choice voting and a hearing calendar.
minutes.summary: A short meeting with four members absent. The chair presented new write-in candidate wording from Carl Luck, a proposal to hear about ranked choice voting, the enforcement section, and a calendar of public hearings leading to the May 2019 Town Meeting. No votes were taken apart from adjournment.

decisions.decision: The write-in candidate wording will go on a future agenda for discussion, and Carl will be told it is coming back.
The park, cemetery and sewer committees will be given the option to come and talk to the committee once the simplified language is sent.
The committee will do outreach to the housing authority about the duties listed in the Charter.
The October 10th meeting will finalize and vote on the material for the special town meeting report.

Revised write-in candidate wording from a resident will go on a future agenda for discussion, and he will be told it is coming back.
The October 10th meeting is set to finalize and vote on the material for the special town meeting report.
Park, cemetery and sewer committees will be offered the chance to speak to the committee once simplified language is sent to them.

why_it_matters: The Charter is the town's governing document, and the changes this committee drafts, including write-in rules and the duties of boards, are what residents would be asked to vote on at Town Meeting.
Nothing was decided at this meeting, so the public hearings leading to the May 2019 Town Meeting are the point where residents can still shape the wording.
